"description": "Exports artwork to a file, returns it as a stream, or uploads it to an Adobe-hosted URL. Supports raster formats (PNG, JPEG, TIFF, PSD, WEBP, BMP), vector formats (SVG, PDF, EPS, DWG, DXF), and native Illustrator format (AI). Target what to export: CANVAS (entire document, default), ARTBOARD (single artboard by index), UUID (specific objects by uuid \u2014 no selection needed), or SELECTION (currently selected objects). Output goes to one of three places: provide `outputPath` for file mode (default), `outputMode='stream'` for inline data (PNG/SVG only), or `uploadTo` for a direct upload to a presigned URL. For the presigned-upload flow: obtain uploadTo from the host's canvas-upload preparation step and pass it here exactly as given; leave authBearer unset \u2014 a presigned URL already carries its own signature, and adding a Bearer header breaks it. No `url` is returned in `details` for this path (it's a raw-byte PUT, not a harness POST); success just means the bytes are uploaded, and the caller resolves the final asset URL in a separate step. Never guess a value for uploadTo/authBearer yourself. For file mode, provide outputPath with a full path. Host OS comes only from client_platform on each prompt (macos|windows) \u2014 never infer OS from user path syntax. Passing a group or layer UUID exports all children within that container. Omit optional styling parameters (antiAlias, backgroundColor, quality, colorModel, etc.) unless the user explicitly asked for them \u2014 when omitted, the user's saved Export Preferences are used. Never guess their values. Do not use this tool for a Save or Save As request \u2014 exporting is not saving.",

"description": "Extract named resources ('what': colors, swatches, symbols, brushes, graphic-styles, character-styles, or paragraph-styles) from a document at an absolute file path into the current document. 'filters' is an optional comma-separated list narrowing results; allowed values depend on 'what' (brushes: used,unused,calligraphic,scatter,art,bristle,pattern; symbols: used,unused,static,dynamic; graphic-styles/character-styles/paragraph-styles: used,unused; colors/swatches: used,unused,process,global,spot,solid,pattern,linear-gradient,radial-gradient,gradient). A result only carries the fields for axes you actually filtered: omitting an axis skips its field (and, for usage, its scan) -- cheapest, still matches everything; giving any value(s) from an axis (even all of them) adds that axis's field ('type' or 'used') to every result. So to learn everything about a 'what' with full classification in one call, list every value of the axis/axes you need rather than omitting them (e.g. filters=\\\"used,unused,static,dynamic\\\" for symbols) -- free for kind/type, but usage costs a full document scan, so skip both used/unused if you don't need that field. Notes: process+global = solid colors only (excludes gradients/patterns; solid+pattern+gradient = all); prefer 'gradient' over listing linear-gradient+radial-gradient together; never combine 'gradient' with either subtype (it already implies both); 'spot' is a subset of 'global' -- don't combine them. Always pass dryRun:true unless the user explicitly wants the resources copied into the current document -- omitting dryRun (or passing false) performs a real, document-mutating extraction, not a preview. Any list/what/show/describe/summarize-style question about a file's contents requires dryRun:true, even when falling back to Extract after a different tool (e.g. an attachment-inspection or summarization agent) failed to answer that same question -- a failed prior tool does not turn a listing request into an import request. dryRun never modifies anything and honors 'filters' identically. Never call Extract without dryRun more than once per request for the same 'what', and don't fall back to a different/empty filter just to keep exploring; a 0-result response is final. If an unfiltered dryRun for a 'what' already returns 0, that 'what' has none in the file -- don't retry with filters. Returns JSON describing the resources that would be (dryRun) or were (real call) extracted.",

"description": "Batch query and update tool for object properties (color, weight, font, text content). "description": "Create or patch a gradient on the fill or stroke of one or more objects.\\n\\nCREATE / REPLACE mode \u2014 provide both colors and positions: builds a new gradient with the given stops, replacing any existing one.\\nPATCH mode \u2014 omit both colors and positions: preserves all existing stops (including midpoints), gradient-level properties (interpolation, dither), and geometry (origin, length, matrix). "description": "Traces a raster or placed image into vectors with Image Trace, or expands an existing live Image Trace into a final vector group. To preserve the user's original, always DUPLICATE the source image first (e.g. with DuplicateObjects) and run this tool on the duplicate's `uuid` \u2014 never trace the original directly. Offset the duplicate so it sits BESIDE the original with a small gap \u2014 not overlapping it (e.g. DuplicateObjects offsetX/offsetY), keeping it within the canvas bounds where possible. (This applies only when `uuid` is a source raster/placed image; when it is already a live tracing you are re-tracing or expanding, operate on it directly \u2014 do not duplicate.) Before tracing, determine what the image actually is \u2014 its content is NOT in the object metadata, so do not guess from it. Unless you have already seen the image this turn, inspect the actual pixels first \u2014 the selected image, or the whole canvas when nothing is selected \u2014 using whatever image-inspection capability you have, then pass the `preset` that matches what you saw. If no preset matches the requested look or exact settings, pick the CLOSEST one, run it as `trace_live` (re-runnable, so the user can review), and say clearly in your reply which preset you used and that it's the closest approximation, not exact. `action` controls the result: by default it stays a LIVE, editable Image Trace (`trace_live`); it is expanded into a final vector group only when the user asks. "description": "Get detailed visual appearance properties for one or more objects. Response format: {success, details, visual_appearance: [{uuid, properties: {fill_stack, stroke_stack, has_fill, has_stroke, opacity, blend_mode, graphic_style, mask_context, is_clip_path, hidden, locked}}, ...]}. Each result includes: fill_stack (array), stroke_stack (array), has_fill (boolean), has_stroke (boolean), opacity (number), blend_mode (string), graphic_style (string|null), mask_context (object with is_clipping_mask and clipped_by), is_clip_path (boolean \u2014 true when this path is the clipping mask path inside a clipping group), hidden (boolean), locked (boolean). For gradient fills/strokes, the color entry includes: model='gradient', gradientType, angle, length, origin, and a stops array where each stop has rampPoint (0-100), midPoint, opacity, and a color object. To change only angle or gradientType on an existing gradient, use SetGradient PATCH mode (omit colors+positions entirely \u2014 no need to read stops first). To replace stops while keeping the same count/positions as a reference, read the stops here then rebuild colors[] from each stop's color field and positions[] from each stop's rampPoint, and pass them to SetGradient CREATE mode. Use this when you need to analyze visual styling. To confirm a color/appearance-named target, call this with the candidate UUIDs. BATCH PROCESSING: When analyzing multiple objects, pass array of UUIDs to get all results in one call. LARGE RESPONSES: When results exceed the size limit, partial results are returned with truncated=true and resume_hint with instructions on how to continue.",

"description": "Get recursive structure for one or more objects (including layers). Returns 'structures' array. Each entry: uuid, name, object_type, bounds, locked (when true), hidden (when true) \u2014 both inherited from ancestors; is_generative (when true), generative_type (when present), has_edit_lineage (when true). Bounds are visual bounds that include live effect expansion (e.g. Gaussian blur expands bounds beyond the path geometry). Bounds may be absent for empty groups. Text objects also include text_content (the full text string). Groups and layers have children (array, z-order: 0=topmost) and child_count. Use maxDepth to limit recursion (groups/layers at max depth show child_count + child_types summary instead of children). Use includeTypes to filter \u2014 only matching types appear; groups/layers are always traversed to find matches within the traversed depth. NOTE: includeTypes only matches objects reached within maxDepth \u2014 if matching objects exist inside nested groups beyond maxDepth they will not appear. Use maxDepth=-1 to find all matching objects regardless of nesting. Example: maxDepth=2, includeTypes=['text'] finds text objects up to 2 levels deep. CRITICAL: Use this to drill into groups and layers from GetCanvasStructure/GetArtboardStructure. BATCH: Pass array of UUIDs. LARGE RESPONSES: When the response size limit is reached, expansion stops \u2014 groups already listed retain child_count/child_types for navigation. Results include truncated=true and resume_hint. RESUME: truncation can happen at ANY depth, not just the top level a UUID was requested with \u2014 recursively scan every node in 'structures' (including nested 'children', however deep) for partial:true and resume EACH one individually via uuids=[that node's uuid], startAfterUuid=<its resume_after_uuid> (see the startAfterUuid parameter for how multiple uuids/cursors combine in one call). If a node has partial:true but NO resume_after_uuid, either that group's expansion stopped before any child was returned, or (for a text object) its text_content was dropped to fit the size limit (text_length still reflects the true length) \u2014 either way, retry with uuids=[that uuid] and no startAfterUuid to get it fresh with its own budget. A uuid in remaining_uuids that is NOT itself marked partial anywhere was never touched at all \u2014 re-call with uuids=[that uuid] alone, no cursor needed. RESUME PATTERN \u2014 to FULLY expand a list of uuids you MUST drain BOTH mechanisms until nothing is truncated or partial. A single response can carry remaining_uuids AND nested partial:true nodes at the same time; handling only one leaves objects uncollected. Keep two queues: 'cursored' (partial nodes to resume, each with its own resume_after_uuid) and 'fresh' (uuids not yet reached, seeded with the uuids you want to expand). Loop until both are empty. Example Python:\\ndef find_partials(nodes):\\n    found, stack = [], list(nodes or [])\\n    while stack:\\n        n = stack.pop()\\n        if n.get(\\\"partial\\\"):\\n            found.append((n[\\\"uuid\\\"], n.get(\\\"resume_after_uuid\\\")))\\n        stack.extend(n.get(\\\"children\\\") or [])\\n    return found\\ncursored, fresh, structures = [], list(target_uuids), []\\nwhile cursored or fresh:\\n    kwargs = {\\\"includeTypes\\\": [\\\"text\\\"], \\\"maxDepth\\\": \\\"-1\\\"}\\n    if cursored:\\n        uuid, cursor = cursored.pop(0)\\n        kwargs[\\\"uuids\\\"] = [uuid] + fresh\\n        fresh = []\\n        if cursor:\\n            kwargs[\\\"startAfterUuid\\\"] = cursor\\n    else:\\n        kwargs[\\\"uuids\\\"], fresh = fresh, []\\n    res = GetObjectStructure(**kwargs)\\n    structures.extend(res.get(\\\"structures\\\") or [])\\n    cursored += find_partials(res.get(\\\"structures\\\") or [])\\n    fresh += res.get(\\\"remaining_uuids\\\") or []\\nThen filter 'structures' (recursively over children) by object_type for your target objects.",

"description": "Cleans up messy or hand-drawn paths by reducing anchor points and/or smoothing jaggedness. This EDITS geometry \u2014 it approximates the original shape within a tolerance, it does not preserve it exactly. Higher curvePrecision / lower smoothingPercentage = closer to the original but less cleanup; lower curvePrecision / higher smoothingPercentage = more aggressive cleanup but more shape drift. mode='simplify': reduces the number of anchor points within a curve-fit tolerance (same as Object > Path > Simplify) \u2014 use when a path has too many/dense anchor points. In mode='simplify' (only), pointsAfter is guaranteed never to exceed pointsBefore: at a very high curvePrecision the curve-fit can technically need more anchors than it started with, in which case that path is left as it was rather than made worse. If pointsAfter equals pointsBefore, pass a lower curvePrecision and re-call to actually reduce anchors \u2014 omitting curvePrecision uses the application's Simplify preference (often high/conservative) and will not by itself reduce anchors further. mode='smooth': repositions anchor points/handles to remove jaggedness WITHOUT reducing point count (same as the Smooth tool) \u2014 use when lines look jagged, rough, or hand-drawn. mode='both' (default): smooths first, then simplifies the result \u2014 use for general 'clean up this path' / 'make the lines cleaner' requests. The pointsAfter<=pointsBefore guarantee above only covers the simplify step itself; if smoothing increases anchor count, the final pointsAfter can still exceed the original pointsBefore. curvePrecision/angleThreshold/smoothingPercentage are optional. When curvePrecision is omitted, the application's Simplify preference (GetTolerance) is used. When angleThreshold is omitted, the application's Simplify preference (GetAngleThresold) is used. When smoothingPercentage is omitted, it auto-calibrates per path (same as the Smooth tool's default). Only affects anchors that are curve points; anchors explicitly marked as corner points (e.g. straight polygon-style paths with no curve handles) are intentionally left untouched by design \u2014 this matches Illustrator's own Simplify/Smooth, which never round off a rectangle's corners either. If a call reports success but pointsBefore equals pointsAfter with no meaningful bounds change, the path is likely all corner points and not a candidate for cleanup. Only path objects with 3+ anchor points are eligible \u2014 groups, compound paths, text, and paths with fewer anchors are skipped, not treated as failures (reported in `results` with skipped=true and a reason). For groups, use GetObjectStructure to expand to path children first, then pass those uuids \u2014 compound paths and text cannot be decomposed into individual paths by any tool and are simply not supported. Returns per-object anchor-point counts and bounding boxes before/after \u2014 YOU are responsible for checking that delta and re-calling with lower precision/percentage (or telling the user) if the shape drifted more than intended; the tool does not enforce shape fidelity itself.",

"description": "Single-traversal production QA inspection of the active document. Walks the art tree once and returns a categorized JSON report of findings aggregated by issue tag, each with a display_name, count, and affected_objects[] array; UUIDs and raw fact fields (effective PPI, stroke widths, font license types, etc.) are per affected object, not per aggregated finding. Available scopes: document (color mode, profile, bleed, units, metadata, artboard checks), images (resolution, embedded size, pixel dimensions, color space, missing embedded ICC on linked placed rasters), links (broken, modified, damaged), text (fonts: missing, embeddability, license; text frames: overset, sizing, scaling, leading), colors (fill/stroke colors, spot colors, strokes, overprint white/black/non-black, rich black CMYK detection, raster effects), objects (scale, visibility, position, empty groups, locked state, objects near trim edge / bleed extension). Only the requested scopes are executed and emitted in the response \u2014 use this to focus on a specific concern and reduce response size. Omit `scopes` (or pass an empty array) to run all domains. Response shape: top-level `checks` object keyed by category (document/images/links/text/colors/objects), each with a `findings` array (+ optional `partial: true`); top-level `summary` object holds counts and context (total_issues, categories_with_issues, document_context, scopes). `details` is a short human-readable status line (e.g. \\\"findings=3 categories=2\\\") meant for logging/display. Read findings from `checks.<category>.findings` and counts from `summary`. Tool returns raw facts only \u2014 findings are pre-aggregated by issue tag with `display_name` and `affected_objects[]`. No severity in JSON. PREFLIGHT SEVERITY: Classify per the user's stated output moment (print/export/share/screen). If the user did not state a moment, derive it from the document context in the response: is_print_doc=true \u2192 treat as print; is_print_doc=false \u2192 treat as screen. If is_print_doc is absent or ambiguous, default to print. Always state which moment you assumed and why. Must fix: the violation is irreversible at output time regardless of designer intent. Needs review: threshold violated but correctness depends on designer intent or context. Always classify as Needs review regardless of output moment: text_size_minimum, stroke_hairline, dash_too_short, overprint_on_non_black, zero_dimension_object, object_too_close_to_trim_edge. What's fine: positive observations (e.g. fonts present, color mode correct) \u2014 derive from what the tool did NOT report; never place failed findings here; omit this section entirely when you have no positive observations to make. Scope selection from the user's prompt: targeted request that names ONE attribute \u2192 pass matching `scopes` and report ONLY that attribute (do NOT expand into adjacent prepress checks even if returned; surface any extras as a single footnote line). Multi-attribute request (2+ named attributes, e.g. 'check color mode, bleed, spot colors, and hairline strokes') \u2192 pass all matching scopes for ALL named attributes; Broad request ('full preflight', 'list issues by severity', 'is this file good to go', or no specific attribute) \u2192 omit `scopes` and report EVERY finding the tool returned. Tool returns raw facts only \u2014 findings are pre-aggregated by issue tag with `display_name` and `affected_objects[]`. No severity in JSON. Agent classifies each finding per the SCOPE DISCIPLINE \u2014 PREFLIGHT SEVERITY policy in the system prompt. Each affected_objects[] entry contains uuid (when object-scoped), name, and issue-specific raw fields (e.g., effective_ppi, stroke_width, font_family). checks_skipped: optional array of checks that could not run due to suite errors or unavailability. Each entry has 'check' (tag) and 'reason'. IMPORTANT: an empty findings category is only trustworthy when checks_skipped contains no entry for that category. Final response (agent narrative): open with one sentence using `total_issues` from the summary (count of distinct issue types) and the output moment (e.g. '8 issues need attention before printing.'). Then emit up to 3 labelled sections in this order: **Critical Issues: N**, **Warnings: N**, and **Passed Checks** (no count \u2014 derived from absences of failed findings in scopes that were actually run; reference `checks_skipped` to avoid claiming a check passed when it was skipped). Skip **Critical Issues** or **Warnings** when N = 0. If Critical Issues and Warnings are both zero say 'Your file is production ready. No issues found.' and still include the Passed Checks section listing what was verified. Each finding (and each Passed Checks entry) is a single numbered line: N. {display_name} \u2014 {one-line action or consequence, or for Passed Checks: one-line confirmation of what passed}. No sub-lists. No bold heading per finding. No emojis. Restart numbering at 1 in Warnings and Passed Checks. Do NOT replace the numbered-list-of-findings with a single markdown table whose rows are the findings themselves; a per-finding affected-objects table as supplementary detail beneath a numbered finding line is OK, but the numbered line is required. Severity classification is principle-based (output moment + missing/render-breaking vs context-dependent) per the system prompt's PREFLIGHT SEVERITY policy \u2014 do not consult a static issue-to-tier table. Does not cover vision-only checks (contrast, visual alignment) or checks needing export-format context (transparency flattening). Use this for ANY readiness/verification request \u2014 prompts phrased with check / inspect / audit / verify / validate against document attributes (color mode, profile, bleed, resolution, units, artboard sizes, hidden or locked layers within export-range artboards, fonts, linked images, embedded images, text sizing/overset, spot colors, hairline strokes, overprint, transparency), as well as bare 'check this' / 'run a preflight' / 'production QA' / 'is it ready for print|export|share' / 'verify ... for print output'.",

"description": "Places (embeds or links) a raster or vector image into the document at specified coordinates with optional sizing. Supports AI, AVIF, BMP, EPS, GIF, HEIC/HEIF, JPEG/JPG, PDF, PNG, PSD, TIF/TIFF, and WEBP for linking and embedding. Supports CDR, CGM, DOC, DOCX, DWG, DXF, RTF, SVG, SVGZ, and TXT for embedding only. For multi-page PDFs and AI files, use `page` (1-based) to select a specific page; defaults to page 1 if omitted. (x, y) is the top-left corner. If position omitted, image is centered on the active artboard. Aspect ratio is always preserved. Coordinates are canvas-global in points with Y-down. Replace-object workflow (e.g. placing a Firefly-edited image back): (1) record the original object's uuid, (2) call PlaceImage with position='above:<original-uuid>' while the original still exists, (3) then call DeleteObjects on the original \u2014 never delete first or PlaceImage will fail with 'Reference object not found', and a retry without position will default to front and corrupt z-order. "description": "Rasterizes one or more vector/text/group objects (by UUID) into a single raster image, mirroring Object > Rasterize. The source objects are replaced by the new raster when disposal succeeds \u2014 their input UUIDs are then unusable; use the returned `uuid` instead of retrying them. Returns the `uuid` of the created raster, or the mask group when `createMask` is true (uuid may be omitted if all post-commit response serialization attempts fail). Color mode and resolution default to the document's settings; anti-aliasing defaults to artOptimized. Rejected if: any UUID is unknown, unresolvable, or an empty string; any UUID refers to a layer; any object is locked or hidden; all resolved objects are children of a perspective object (pass the perspective object's UUID instead); or the combined bounding box is empty. When createMask is true: also rejected if any target cannot contribute usable outline geometry (raster images, text, symbol, or graph objects, or groups and plugin art with no usable path descendants; placed images and mesh objects are supported). A failure leaves the document unchanged, except when createMask is true: once the mask group is created the tool returns success, and the only remaining failure is a rare internal 'mask not produced' error that leaves the document changed (undo to revert). On the no-mask path, if at least one source is disposed but later disposals fail, the tool still returns success=true with a partial-failure note in details; the document is in a partial state \u2014 use Undo and re-attempt with the original selection.",

"description": "Remaps the color palette of vector artwork objects as a group using a Firefly-generated palette driven by a theme or mood prompt \u2014 use for palette, mood, tone, aesthetic, or style changes (e.g. 'make it warmer', 'recolor to autumn', 'more vibrant', 'ocean-like', 'cyberpunk neon'). Extracts prominent colors across all objects and remaps them together, preserving visual relationships. Use only for open-ended mood/theme changes: it generates a palette and cannot hit an exact value. If the request names the literal color(s) to end up with \u2014 a hex, a Pantone/spot name, 'all red', or a color space like 'grayscale'/'black and white' \u2014 use SetAppearance instead. The response's resultingColors field lists the distinct new colors the engine produced and applied (across all recolored objects, symbol instances and mesh nodes included). It is the authoritative record of the applied colors: read it to judge whether the palette matches the request, not what you expected.
